patch_description: The original program failed validation because it fundamentally violated the output contract and data-preservation rules: it added an extra "original_index" column, dropped/merged cells via merge, left the returned `column_orderings` as an empty list (invalid per-row orderings), sorted rows destroying row identity, and built a fragile value-grouping recursion (attribute-based `getattr(row, col)`, `df.stack()` Counters) that altered/dropped data and could crash. The fix replaces the algorithm with a correct, bounded construction: serialize all cells once, build three candidate per-row column orderings — (1) a global order ranked by sum len(v)*count(v)*(count(v)-1), (2) an alternative len-weighted pair-repetition ranking, and (3) a recursive conditional partition tree that branches on the column with the largest length-weighted repeated-pair savings inside each group — then score each candidate with the exact ideal character-Trie reuse (sum of LCPs of lexicographically adjacent serialized rows, computed with C-speed slice comparisons and binary-search LCP), select the best, and emit a per-row permuted DataFrame (object dtype, all original values preserved) plus matching per-row column orderings. Column merges and one-way dependencies are honored as adjacency constraints in each row's ordering. No extra columns, no dropped rows, no fabricated values.
